story: Gary and Donna are standing together on Magnolia Loop under the bright 76-degree sunshine, trading friendly jabs about a tennis date at ten tomorrow while Gary tries to get Hal's attention for a cart paperwork question. Donna is determined to lock Gary in and has named Hal as her witness, while Hal, watchful as ever, raises the matter of too many flamingos on the lawns and asks to settle it neighbor to neighbor before Friday dinner. Back in her kitchen, Rosa is cheerfully optimistic as she checks her pantry and fridge against her shopping list and circles what she still needs to buy today.
events: Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the pantry and fridge against my shopping list, then circle what I need to buy today

gary.thought_process: Donna already offered tomorrow at ten for pickleball practice and I haven't actually answered her yet. Hal just showed up, and he's the one who's going to check my cart paperwork line by line before Architectural Review. Best move is to answer Donna quickly and warmly, then turn to Hal about the filing. I'll address Donna first since her question is still hanging, and mention Hal is just in time so the paperwork conversation follows naturally next tick.

parameters.content: Ten tomorrow works, Donna. Fair warning, I'll be the one apologizing to the ball. And Hal, good timing, I've got my cart paperwork to run past you when you've got a minute.

donna.thought_process: Gary replied to my paddle invitation but only talked about cart lights and Friday dinner, so he never actually answered about tomorrow at ten. I shouldn't re-ask word for word, but I can pin him down in a friendly way, since this is a sound moment to lock in practice. Hal just arrived too, and he'll want to hear about it, which helps my social-chair standing. Cornbread is a nice touch, so I'll acknowledge dinner briefly and steer back to the courts.

parameters.content: Cornbread, bless you, Rosa will love it. Now don't dodge me, Gary: ten o'clock tomorrow at the courts, paperwork can wait an hour. Hal, you're our witness.

hal.thought_process: I've come out to Magnolia Loop with the violation notebook in mind. Gary and Donna are both right here, and Donna's flamingo flock is in plain view, so I can do my count honestly and in the open. L-02 says three ornaments max visible from the street, and a fair count beats a complaint behind someone's back. I'm looking forward to Friday dinner at Rosa's, so I'll keep it dry rather than hostile. Best move is to talk to Donna about the flock directly, give her a chance to get under the limit before anything goes to the committee.

parameters.content: Afternoon, Donna. I count more flamingos than the ordinance allows. Three is the limit from the street, and I'd rather settle it neighbor to neighbor than send it to the committee. Can we sort that out before Friday dinner?

rosa.thought_process: I've already checked my shift schedule, counted chairs, set out plates, and written the menu and shopping list. Nobody's nearby, and it's a sunny Thursday noon. The only thing left on the Friday dinner is actually buying the groceries, but the kitchen is the object I can touch right now. I should stop re-checking things I've already handled and do something productive: go over the shopping list once more against the pantry so I know exactly what to grab, then get moving. Friday is tomorrow, so the list needs to turn into groceries today.

parameters.content: Check the pantry and fridge against my shopping list, then circle what I need to buy today

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
